metadata.note: Modern-day Muni Cable Car network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://muni-gtfs.apps.sfmta.com/data/muni_gtfs-current.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added from SFMTA, Market Street Railway and Wikipedia sources, tracing the lines back to the 1870s-1880s cable car boom that followed Hallidie's 1873 Clay Street Hill Railroad, the world's first cable car line. Note the REAL two-year gap 1982-1984, when the entire system was shut down for a complete rebuild and no cable cars ran at all. Unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, the older headway_min values are estimates, not real timetables.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.line: Muni Cable Car: California Street Cable Car

segments.note: The California Street Cable Railroad opened in 1878, five years after Andrew Hallidie's Clay Street Hill Railroad proved the technology - the world's first cable car line, which began public service Sept 1 1873 after its Aug 2 trial run. estimated era boundary/frequency based on researched milestone; no historical timetable found.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its dates and service. Supporting references for the line:
https://muni-gtfs.apps.sfmta.com/data/muni_gtfs-current.zip

segments.note: The Apr 18 1906 earthquake and fire devastated the cable car system; many ruined lines were rebuilt as electric streetcars instead, and only the steepest routes came back as cable. estimated era boundary/frequency based on researched milestone; no historical timetable found.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its dates and service. Supporting references for the line:

segments.note: Mayor Lapham moved to shut the system down in 1947, but Friedel Klussmann's Citizens' Committee to Save the Cable Cars put Measure 10 on the ballot, and it passed Nov 4 1947 by 166,989 to 51,457, obliging the city to keep operating them. The system was made a 'moving' National Historic Landmark Oct 1 1964. estimated era boundary/frequency based on researched milestone; no historical timetable found.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its dates and service. Supporting references for the line:

segments.note: The entire system shut down in 1982 for a total rebuild - 69 blocks of track and cable channel replaced, the car barn and powerhouse rebuilt, 37 cars repaired - and full service returned Jun 21 1984 with a ribbon-cutting at Union Square and a parade up Powell Street. (Real 2-year gap precedes this segment.) estimated era boundary/frequency based on researched milestone; no historical timetable found.
